tex_content.html:
Corollary
↗ prop:schur-lemma 1. ch7:7.20

If $(M,g)$ is a connected Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$, then $g$ is Einstein if and only if \[ \stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}=0. \]

Proof

\sketch If $\mathrm{Rc}=\lambda g$, then tracing gives $\lambda =S/n$, so $\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}=0$. Conversely, vanishing traceless Ricci gives $\mathrm{Rc}=(S/n)g$, and Schur’s lemma makes $S/n$ constant.

□

On a Lorentzian $4$-manifold, the Einstein field equation has the form \begin{equation} \mathrm{Rc}-\tfrac 12Sg=T, \tag {7.35} \end{equation} where $T$ is a symmetric $2$-tensor. In vacuum, $T=0$; tracing (7.35) in dimension $4$ gives $S=2S$, hence $S=0$ and $\mathrm{Rc}=0$. With a cosmological term $\Lambda g$ on the left, the vacuum equation instead has the form $\mathrm{Rc}=\lambda g$ for a constant $\lambda $.
